the identification of a novel gene involved in PCD and with its function in the assembly of dynein arm complexes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LRRC50 is essential for the preassembly of the outer dynein arms, and its absence causes a severe form of PCD.

loss-of-function mutations of the gene LRRC50, encoding a leucine-rich repeat containing protein, are responsible for a new PCD subtype, characterized by the absence both of outer and inner dynein arms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LRRC50, which is conserved from protists to humans, is essential for the formation of the outer dynein arm in motile ciliogenesis.
the LRRC50 gene is the first gene identified in humans to encode a protein that is involved in the preassembly of dyenins, a key step in ciliary assembly.
the identification of LRRC50 as the gene responsible for a PCD phenotype is a major step forward in understanding the molecular basis of this disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of a PCD-causing mutation in a gene encoding an assembly factor of the dynein arm is a paradigm for the identification of new genes responsible for ciliary diseases.
the identification of new PCD genes in humans may be facilitated through the use of Chlamyomona reinhardtii mutants.
the human LRRC50 gene is a new PCD gene, and it is likely that other genes encoding proteins with a similar function will be found in the future.
